rankingCriteria: information gain, safety, cost, prerequisite readiness, and whether the outcome would change a decision. Rank 1 is highest.
carriedOver: BL-002..BL-012 from RUN-20260807-1 remain open and unchanged except BL-001 (closed: the reimplementation was commissioned and completed; superseded by BL-013) and BL-004 (still open; recurred this run as PROV-008).

items.title: Commission the independent implementation's re-run against protocol v1.1.0, on a machine that does not hold the reference
items.hypothesis: R1-R4 close the 22,440-world conclusion divergence: the re-run reproduces the reference's conclusion distribution on all 110,840 receipt-producing worlds and reproduces C11's pinned contentDigest.
items.discriminatingTest: Diff conclusion distributions world-class by world-class and compare the C11 digest byte-for-byte. Any residual disagreement localises a new ambiguity; a digest mismatch localises a canonicalisation misreading.
items.whyItMatters: KL-000's registered next gate, KL-011's binding prerequisite, and the direct test of whether the specification loop converges. Owner commission; explicitly NOT executable by this repository's agents (an in-house re-run of impl-rs would be agreement worth nothing).
items.wouldChangeWhat: Pass makes verified-independent claimable (owner promotion) and unblocks KL-011 preregistration. Fail reopens the specification loop or KL-000 itself.
items.cost: repo-side: one commission-package commit (artifacts as roles, not paths -- IND-101). Commission-side: implementer time on a clean machine.

items.title: v1.2.0 repair bundle: world-referential I2/I5, baseline dedup, fixture-note correction, one vocabulary
items.hypothesis: Restating I2 and I5 world-referentially (F1/F2), resolving B2 vs B3 (F3), correcting C06's note (F13), documenting F14, and unifying registration ids with report keys (NAM-101) removes every known vacuously-satisfiable invariant without moving any number.
items.discriminatingTest: Same discipline as v1.1.0: register an exact-equality prediction table, re-run in full, halt on any moved number. Additionally B2 must then fail registered I2 as literally read.
items.whyItMatters: F1 is measured, not hypothetical: the registered must-fail baseline B2 records zero violations of literal I2 across all 176,120 worlds. A cross-system transaction (KL-011) inherits every receipt-internal hole.
items.wouldChangeWhat: Whether KL-011's preregistration can cite invariants with actual power against dishonest evaluators.
items.cost: one registration + one ~90s re-run; zero spend
items.prerequisitesNote: SEQUENCED AFTER BL-013: the commission target must not move while the implementer is working.

items.title: Pin margin semantics and conversionsToReverse (F4/F5)
items.hypothesis: Registering margin's sign convention (reference: absolute) and conversionsToReverse's definition including the empty-ledger and negative-margin cases removes the last receipt fields with cross-implementation ambiguity, affecting 38,760 worlds' receipts under the rejected reading.
items.discriminatingTest: A fixture with opposing > supporting pins the sign; a fixture with an empty ledger pins (or corrects) the conversionsToReverse=1 edge the independent implementer flagged as arguably wrong.
items.whyItMatters: C11 was deliberately sign-agnostic to avoid resolving this by the back door; that leaves it genuinely unresolved, and it is the largest remaining receipt-divergence surface (22.0% of exhaustive worlds).
items.wouldChangeWhat: Owner decision required on the sign convention and on whether an empty ledger's conversionsToReverse should be 1, 0, or refused -- the independent implementer's analysis gives the options.

items.title: Make the randomized phase cross-implementation comparable (F11/SPEC-102)
items.hypothesis: Registering a draw schedule (or adopting the independent implementation's worldStreamHash primitive) turns the randomized phase from a replication into a reproduction between implementations.
items.discriminatingTest: Two implementations produce identical worldStreamHash values for the frozen seed, or the registration is amended to drop the unverifiable cross-implementation invalidation clause.
items.whyItMatters: The million-world phase currently contributes nothing to cross-implementation claims except a rate. worldStreamHash is also independently valuable evidence of the reimplementation's design quality, worth adopting rather than reinventing.

items.title: Specify the adversarial phase instead of naming a test file (F12)
items.hypothesis: Registering the ten attacks as specifications (attack class, input construction, required outcome) makes phase 4 reproducible from the protocol, which RESEARCH-METHOD.md requires and v1.0.0/v1.1.0 do not satisfy.
items.discriminatingTest: A clean-room reader constructs the attack suite from the registration alone and reaches the same ten required outcomes.
items.whyItMatters: The adversarial phase is currently defined by reference to code -- the one thing a preregistration exists not to do. The independent implementer had to invent its own ten attacks, so the two adversarial results are not comparable at all.

items.title: Fifth ablation: an evaluator that drops opposing roots from the receipt
items.hypothesis: A B6 that omits opposingRoots converts counterexamples into silence while passing receipt-internal I5; it gives the suite power against the F2 hole that no current baseline exercises (I5a and I5b are identical on B1-B4).
items.discriminatingTest: B6 must be caught by world-referential I5 and by nothing receipt-internal -- demonstrating the F2 gap and its repair simultaneously.
items.whyItMatters: The positive-control table currently has no power against the exact failure mode (suppressing counterexamples) that matters most for absence claims.
items.cost: ~20 lines + registration entry, part of v1.2.0
items.prerequisitesNote: with BL-014, since it is only meaningful once I5 has a world-referential form

items.title: Specification-package hygiene: artifacts as roles, contamination check for structure as well as numbers
items.hypothesis: A packaging checklist (redact paths to roles; grep the package for reference identifiers AND reference structure; record package digests at handoff) prevents the IND-101 class of leak.
items.discriminatingTest: Apply the checklist to the v1.1.0 commission package; the OPERATOR-DISCLOSURE.md leak class (paths in an artifacts list) must be caught mechanically before handoff.
items.whyItMatters: The operator's number-contamination check passed while five reference paths sat in the package. Structure leaks and value leaks are different checks and only one existed.
